page-begin-meta-description: Last looked at Ethereum a few years ago? A lot has changed. Here's what Ethereum is today, what people use it for, and how to get involved.
page-begin-hero-description: If your picture of Ethereum is from a few years ago, you're not alone. A lot has changed. Here's the short version: what Ethereum is today, what people use it for, and where you fit in.
page-begin-changed-description: Many people last looked at Ethereum between 2018 and 2020. Since then, the network has been upgraded many times.
page-begin-changed-caption: How Ethereum has changed since 2018 to 2020
page-begin-changed-energy-now: Ethereum replaced mining with staking in 2022, cutting energy use by over 99.9%.
page-begin-changed-ux-now: Better UX: some wallets integrate trading and lending, letting you manage more of your finances in one place.
page-begin-changed-uses-then: Known for token sales and collectibles
page-begin-changed-uses-now: Digital identity and open-source funding, alongside stablecoins and payments. Decentralized finance lets you lend, borrow and trade without a bank.
page-begin-changed-clients-then: Most nodes used the same client
page-begin-changed-clients-now: A broader mix of independent clients, built by different teams.
page-begin-changed-clients-note: Go · Rust · Java · C# · Nim · TypeScript
page-begin-changed-scaling-then: Scaling meant more work for each node
page-begin-changed-scaling-now: Zero-knowledge proofs are being developed to verify transactions with less computing, helping Ethereum handle more activity.
page-begin-misconceptions-description: A lot of what people believe about Ethereum was true a few years ago, or was never the whole story.
page-begin-misconceptions-fees-live: Right now, a typical transaction on Ethereum costs {cost} (median, via growthepie).
page-begin-misconceptions-fees-scale: Businesses that need to run at very large scale can also build their own layer 2 network on top of Ethereum.
page-begin-misconceptions-energy-questio: Doesn't Ethereum use a lot of energy?
page-begin-misconceptions-energy-answer: Not anymore. In 2022, Ethereum replaced mining with staking in an upgrade called The Merge. This cut the network's electricity use by more than 99.988%. Securing the network no longer depends on burning energy. It depends on validators putting ETH at stake.
page-begin-misconceptions-crypto-answer: ETH is the currency that pays for using the network. But Ethereum itself is a shared, programmable platform. Anyone can write a program (a smart contract) that runs on it, and anyone can use it without asking permission. That's why it's home to stablecoins, identity systems and organizations, not just a token.
page-begin-misconceptions-accept-answer: More and more businesses do, mostly through stablecoins. <shopify>Shopify lets merchants accept the USDC stablecoin</shopify>, and <paypal>PayPal launched its own stablecoin, PYUSD, on Ethereum</paypal>. In one 2026 survey, <nca>40% of US crypto holders said they use it to buy goods and services</nca>.
page-begin-misconceptions-scams-question: Isn't it all speculation and scams?
page-begin-misconceptions-scams-answer: It's a fair question. There is speculation, and there are scams, as there are anywhere money moves online. But that's not the whole story. Ethereum is also used to send payments, deliver aid and fund open-source software. And because activity is public, anyone can check what's actually happening.
page-begin-eth-description: ETH is Ethereum's own currency. Here's what people use it for.
page-begin-eth-gas-description: Pay transaction fees (known as gas) for using the network and its apps.
page-begin-eth-money-description: Send and receive money, to anyone, anywhere.
page-begin-eth-collateral-description: Put up collateral to borrow on lending platforms.
page-begin-eth-burn: A portion of every transaction fee is permanently burned. Since 2021, <link>millions of ETH</link> have been removed from circulation.
page-begin-uses-description: Beyond trading, Ethereum is used where people need a shared record that no single party controls.
page-begin-uses-payments-description: Digital dollars that settle in seconds, anywhere. PayPal launched its PYUSD stablecoin on Ethereum.
page-begin-uses-aid-description: Ukraine's Ministry of Digital Transformation used Ethereum to distribute wartime aid to citizens and NGOs.
page-begin-uses-identity-description: Credentials you hold yourself and can prove without oversharing.
page-begin-uses-funding-description: Community grant rounds such as Gitcoin, and Protocol Guild, which funds Ethereum's core contributors.
page-begin-matters-description: Ethereum is built on four principles that only work together. Together they mean you keep the final say over your money, your identity and what you build.
page-begin-matters-open-source-descripti: The systems shaping your life should not be hidden behind closed doors. Ethereum's code can be inspected, verified, and improved by anyone.
page-begin-matters-open-source-proof: In practice: changes are proposed as Ethereum Improvement Proposals (EIPs) and discussed in public, and anyone can propose one. Core clients ship under copyleft and permissive licenses.
page-begin-matters-privacy-description: Your personal life should not become someone else's product. Ethereum lets you interact without handing control of your identity and data to a central platform.
page-begin-matters-censorship-resistance: No company, government, or middleman can freeze you out or block what you build. If you can reach the network, you can use it.
In practice: there's no CEO or board. Nodes are run by people all over the world.
page-begin-matters-security-description: Digital ownership only matters when it cannot be easily taken, altered, or forged. Ethereum is secured by a global network rather than a single organization.
page-begin-matters-security-proof: In practice: the network runs on clients built by separate teams, so no single codebase or company controls it.
page-begin-path-description: Where you go next depends on what brought you here.
page-begin-path-code-description: Build your first smart contract, or contribute to a client.
page-begin-path-research-description: Open problems in cryptography, economics and distributed systems.
page-begin-path-public-sector-title: I work in government or the public sector
page-begin-path-public-sector-descriptio: See how governments and nonprofits use Ethereum.
page-begin-contribute-description: You don't have to wait to get involved. ethereum.org is open source too. It's built and translated by contributors around the world. You can fix a typo, improve a page or help translate it, starting tonight.
